image_description: A close-up view of a human forehead featuring a beige adhesive bandage (Band-Aid) applied horizontally. The bandage has a central white absorbent pad and perforated adhesive wings. The skin texture, pores, and fine hairs are highly detailed, suggesting a macro photography style or high-fidelity generation.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The left adhesive wing exhibits a strange 'melting' or 'smearing' effect where the bandage meets the skin/hairline. The perforations distort and fade into a blurry, undefined mass rather than maintaining a crisp edge or clean tear.
The right edge appears to fuse slightly with the skin texture, lacking a distinct boundary layer. The adhesive texture seems to bleed into the skin pores unnaturally.

The perforation holes on the left side appear warped and inconsistent in size compared to the right side, suggesting a slight failure in maintaining consistent geometric texture mapping across the curved surface.
